newsitem.title: USA: Clinton may name McKinsey's Ferguson to Fed Board.
newsitem.headline: Clinton may name McKinsey's Ferguson to Fed Board.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is expected to name Roger Ferguson, a partner with consulting company McKinsey & Co. Inc., to the Federal Reserve Board if he passes background checks, a U.S. official said on Sunday.
The official said Ferguson, who is black, has a law degree and a doctorate in economics from Harvard University and has specialised in banking as well as payments systems in his work for McKinsey.

Clinton last week approved his staff's recommendations of Ferguson and University of Michigan economist Edward Gramlich for the positions on the central bank's seven-member board and asked that they undergo further background checks.

The U.S. official said that no problems have cropped up so far for either man in the process, which he estimated would take two to three weeks, after which Clinton may choose to make a formal nomination.
He also said that the administration is confident that if they were nominated, both men would be confirmed by the U.S. Senate, which must approve their appointments.

The Federal Reserve's two vacancies opened up earlier this year with the departure of Janet Yellen for the White House Council of Economic Advisers and Lawrence Lindsey for the conservative American Enterprise Institute think tank.

The vacancies came at a sensitive time for the central bank, which last month raised interest rates for the first time in over two years in an effort to head off inflation and keep the economy on track.
The U.S. official said the Clinton administration believed Ferguson and Gramlich would bring a range of experience to the Federal Reserve.

"Gramlich was obviously a very strong academic for us to get and Ferguson provided someone who had some expertise in payment systems (and who had been) a consultant on bank restructuring," the official said.

Gramlich, whose candidacy was disclosed by a U.S. official last Thursday, has been a professor at the University of Michigan for more than 20 years and has served as an acting director of the Congressional Budget Office.
The academic was also in the spotlight earlier this year when a government advisory council that he chaired released a report on ways to shore up the Social Security pension system.

The U.S. official said Ferguson, 45, worked in McKinsey's New York office, where he has done considerable work helping banks prepare themselves to diversify geographically as well as into new products.
He said Ferguson had served as director of research and information systems at McKinsey, where he had also overseen the firm's economic research.
People familiar with the search said the administration was interested in finding a black for one of the Fed postions.

If nominated and confirmed by the Senate, Ferguson would be the third black to serve on the Federal Reserve board, following Emmett Rice, appointed by former President Jimmy Carter, and Andrew Brimmer, named by former President Lyndon Johnson.
